# Job Chapter 19 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 422v–423r

---

**1** Then Job answered and said:

**2** "How long will you torment me and crush me with words? **3** These ten times you have humiliated me; are you not ashamed to wrong me?

**4** And even if it is true that I have erred, my error remains with me. **5** If indeed you exalt yourselves against me and argue my disgrace against me,

**6** know then that God has put me in the wrong, and closed his net around me.

**7** Behold, I cry out, 'Violence!' but I am not answered; I call for help, but there is no justice.

**8** He has walled up my way so that I cannot pass, and he has set darkness upon my paths. **9** He has stripped my glory from me and taken the crown from my head.

**10** He breaks me down on every side, and I am gone; he has uprooted my hope like a tree. **11** He has kindled his wrath against me and counts me as his enemy.

**12** His troops come on together; they have cast up their siege ramp against me and encamp around my tent.

**13** He has put my brothers far from me, and those who knew me are wholly estranged from me. **14** My relatives have failed me, and my close friends have forgotten me. **15** The guests in my house and my maidservants count me as a stranger; I have become a foreigner in their eyes. **16** I call to my servant, but he gives me no answer; I must plead with him with my mouth.

**17** My breath is repulsive to my wife, and I am loathsome to the children of my own family. **18** Even young boys despise me; when I rise, they talk against me. **19** All my closest friends abhor me, and those I loved have turned against me.

**20** My bones cling to my skin and to my flesh, and I have escaped by the skin of my teeth.

**21** Have mercy on me, have mercy on me, O you my friends, for the hand of God has struck me!

**22** Why do you, like God, pursue me? Why are you not satisfied with my flesh?

**23** Oh that my words were written! Oh that they were inscribed in a book! **24** Oh that with an iron pen and lead they were engraved in the rock forever!

**25** For I know that my Redeemer lives, and at the last he will stand upon the earth.

**26** And after my skin has been thus destroyed, yet from my flesh I shall see God, **27** whom I shall see for myself, and my eyes shall behold, and not another. My heart faints within me!

**28** If you say, 'How we will pursue him!' and 'The root of the matter is found in him,' **29** be afraid of the sword yourselves, for wrath brings the punishment of the sword, that you may know there is a judgment."

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

**Verse 20 — "by the skin of my teeth":** One of the most famous idioms in the English language, drawn directly from this verse. In Hebrew, the expression is likely a way of saying "with nothing" — teeth have no skin, so the margin of escape is nonexistent.

**Verses 25-27 — "I know that my Redeemer lives":** The theological summit of the book. The Hebrew *go'el* is a kinsman-redeemer — the family member legally obligated to vindicate, avenge, or redeem a wronged relative. Job's claim that his *go'el* "lives" and will "stand upon the dust" is either (a) a hope for posthumous vindication, (b) an anticipation of bodily resurrection, or (c) a desperate assertion that someone, somewhere, will clear his name. The Christian tradition has read these verses through the lens of resurrection (cf. Handel's Messiah); the Hebrew text is more ambiguous but no less powerful.

**Verse 26 — Textual difficulty:** The Hebrew of this verse is among the most corrupt in the Old Testament. Key questions: Does "from my flesh" mean "while still in my body" or "apart from my body"? Does "after my skin is destroyed" imply death and resurrection or severe illness? Honest translation must acknowledge the ambiguity rather than resolve it.

*— LOGOS*
